tools.when: First thing to try on any packed sample: 'upx -d' either works instantly, or its failure tells you a custom protector needs manual unpacking.

tools.name: RetDec
tools.desc: Avast's free decompiler (CLI + interactive plugin) that turns machine code back into C — ideal for reading the logic of unpacked payloads rather than raw assembly.
tools.when: Read the intent of an unpacked routine — config parsing, anti-debug checks, encryption — as readable C when Ghidra decompilation is not enough detail.
tools.install: pip install retdec-python or download the RetDec release for your platform

tools.name: FLOSS
tools.desc: Obfuscated-string solver that reconstructs stack-assembled and runtime-decoded strings from a sample statically — the unpacking companion that recovers C2 URLs and config keys the packer hid.
tools.when: After upx -d or manual unpacking, run FLOSS to pull the decrypted strings the unpacking stub merely hid in the binary.

domains.name: Purple Team, BAS & Adversary Emulation
domains.tagline: Validate your detections by emulating real adversaries, running atomic TTPs, and mapping coverage against MITRE ATT&CK.

tools.name: MITRE Caldera
tools.desc: Automated adversary emulation platform (now an Apache project) built on ATT&CK: deploy agents, craft adversary profiles from techniques, and run them against your estate.
tools.when: Build a repeatable adversary operation once and re-run it after every detection change or control rollout.

tools.name: Adversary Emulation Library
tools.desc: MITRE Center for Threat-Informed Defense's full (APT29, FIN6, Turla) and micro (webshells, process injection) emulation plans in human-readable plus machine-readable YAML for Caldera.
tools.when: Execute a threat-intel-grounded scenario as a ready-made purple-team script instead of writing one from scratch.

tools.name: PurpleSharp
tools.desc: C# adversary simulation tool that executes ATT&CK-mapped TTPs purely from Windows endpoints (process execution, scheduled tasks, WMI, Kerberos abuse) without needing a C2.
tools.when: Run in-host purple exercises fast: trigger technique sequences and immediately check which SIEM/EDR detections fired.

tools.name: Atomic Red Team
tools.desc: MITRE-aligned library of small, portable detection tests; each atomic test documents a technique's exact procedure plus the logs and telemetry a defender should see if the detection works.
tools.when: Prove a specific detection fires by running the precise TTP procedure it was built to catch.

tools.name: AtomicTestHarnesses
tools.desc: Red Canary's PowerShell module (Python for macOS/Linux) that executes many variations of a single technique and validates the telemetry each variation generates.
tools.when: Check your detections hold up across technique variants, not just the single canonical procedure.

tools.name: Stratus Red Team
tools.desc: Datadog's granular cloud emulation library — 'Atomic Red Team for the cloud' — detonating AWS, Azure, GCP, Entra ID, and K8s techniques mapped to ATT&CK with automatic warmup and cleanup.
tools.when: Validate cloud SIEM detections against real TTPs in a dedicated sandbox cloud account, never production.

tools.name: CloudGoat 2
tools.desc: Rhino Security Labs' 'Vulnerable by Design' AWS/Azure deployment tool that builds intentionally vulnerable, CTF-style scenarios for practicing cloud attack paths.
tools.when: Stand up an authorized practice range in a throwaway cloud account to rehearse TTPs before running real emulation.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK Navigator
tools.desc: Web app for annotating and exploring ATT&CK matrices via shareable layer files; load emulation-plan technique lists to plan what you are about to run.
tools.when: Scope an emulation exercise by marking the techniques on the matrix before touching any platform.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK
tools.desc: The authoritative knowledge base: adversary tactics, techniques, sub-techniques, threat groups, and the data sources needed to detect them.
tools.when: Resolve technique IDs and read detection guidance before any scoring, emulation, or rule building.

tools.name: Infection Monkey
tools.desc: Open-source BAS platform (Guardicore/Akamai) whose agent self-propagates across a network via real exploiters and misconfiguration checks, reporting findings to the Monkey Island console.
tools.when: Automated lateral-movement and control-gap testing on a lab segment or isolated data-center island.

tools.name: OpenBAS
tools.desc: Filigran's open-source breach-and-attack simulation platform (now evolving into OpenAEV) for planning, scheduling, and running adversary-simulation campaigns and crisis exercises.
tools.when: When you need a free multi-team BAS platform that couples technical simulations with exercise tracking, integrated with OpenCTI threat intel.

tools.name: SafeBreach Validate
tools.desc: Commercial BAS pioneer: lightweight simulators on endpoints, network, and cloud run 30,000+ attack methods from its Hacker's Playbook to continuously validate controls.
tools.when: Continuous, enterprise-scale security-control validation when you have budget for a licensed BAS product.

tools.name: AttackIQ
tools.desc: MITRE ATT&CK-aligned BAS platform with a free AttackIQ Flex tier and a large scenario library that continuously exercises prevention, detection, and response controls.
tools.when: Continuous control validation with ATT&CK coverage reporting baked into the vendor platform.

tools.name: Cymulate
tools.desc: BAS platform that deploys lightweight agents to simulate the full kill chain plus exposure management, scoring security posture with prioritized remediation guidance.
tools.when: Benchmark your controls against sector peers and get prioritized gap remediation from one dashboard.

tools.name: DetectionLab
tools.desc: Chris Long's Packer/Vagrant suite that builds a Windows domain pre-loaded with Sysmon, WEF, osquery, and Splunk plus hardened logging defaults (no longer actively maintained since 2023, but still widely used).
tools.when: Spin up a known-good instrumented AD lab to test detections against realistic Windows telemetry.

tools.name: DetectionLab Primer
tools.desc: The official DetectionLab documentation/introduction: architecture, deployment guides for VirtualBox, AWS, Azure, and Hyper-V, and walkthroughs of each pre-installed tool.
tools.when: Read before first build so you pick the right provider and understand what logging you are getting.

tools.name: Splunk Attack Range
tools.desc: Splunk Threat Research Team's Terraform/Ansible range that deploys instrumented AWS/Azure/GCP labs, runs Atomic Red Team and PurpleSharp simulations, and forwards telemetry into Splunk.
tools.when: Develop and CI-test Splunk detections against reproducible attack data in an isolated cloud range.

tools.name: Purple Team Exercise Framework (PTEF)
tools.desc: SCYTHE's industry-standard methodology (v4) for designing purple-team exercises: planning templates, TTP mapping spreadsheets, emulation-plan formats, and a maturity model.
tools.when: Structure your first (or fiftieth) purple exercise so CTI, red, and blue roles, evidence collection, and lessons-learned are all defined up front.

tools.name: OWASP PurpleTeam
tools.desc: OWASP's open purpleteam tooling: an orchestrator with TLS and application scanning components that run coordinated security tests and report results for CI use.
tools.when: Add repeatable purpleteam-style scanning checks to an application/TLS hardening pipeline.

tools.name: DeTT&CT
tools.desc: Rabobank's framework to administer and score data-source quality, visibility, and detection per ATT&CK technique, then export the resulting coverage as ATT&CK Navigator layers.
tools.when: Build a scored, evidence-based map of detection and visibility coverage and prioritize blue-team effort on the gaps.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK Navigator
tools.desc: Web app for annotating and exploring ATT&CK matrices via shareable layer files; load DeTT&CT or VECTR output to render coverage heatmaps.
tools.when: Visualize and communicate detection coverage across the matrix during and after purple exercises.

tools.name: MITRE CAR
tools.desc: MITRE Cyber Analytics Repository: a curated set of analytics, each tied to ATT&CK techniques with data requirements, pseudocode, and reference implementations for validating detections.
tools.when: Find analytics worth implementing when you know which ATT&CK technique you need coverage for.

tools.name: MITRE D3FEND
tools.desc: Counter-adversary engineering knowledge graph of digital artifacts, tactics, and hardening techniques — the defensive counterpart to ATT&CK for describing how countermeasures work.
tools.when: Name and structure defensive countermeasures precisely when documenting what each control actually prevents.

tools.name: MITRE SHIELD
tools.desc: Active defense knowledge base of techniques defenders can use to engage adversaries (deception, hunting, hardening), mapped to ATT&CK for planning proactive defense operations.
tools.when: Plan proactive or deception-based defenses that complement your detection coverage map.

tools.name: yara-x
tools.desc: VirusTotal's Rust rewrite of YARA with a strict compiler that surfaces syntax errors and warnings early, plus a fast CLI for scanning samples with your rules.
tools.when: Compile and regression-test YARA rules in CI — stricter diagnostics catch broken rules before deployment.

tools.name: YARA
tools.desc: The de-facto pattern-matching engine for malware rules; `yara -w` compiles rule sets and flags syntax problems before you scan anything.
tools.when: The baseline check: compile your rules locally and run them against known samples to confirm hits and false positives.

tools.name: CIRCL yara-validator
tools.desc: CIRCL's Python validator that compiles batches of YARA rules, reports which are broken, and attempts automatic repairs on include-related breakage.
tools.when: Bulk-validate a shared rule repository before merging changes.

tools.name: YaraValidator online
tools.desc: Free web validator that compiles rules against current YARA and YARA-X versions to catch compatibility issues without any local install.
tools.when: Instant one-off compatibility check of a rule paste across engine versions.

tools.name: Sigma
tools.desc: Vendor-agnostic detection rule format with a converter ecosystem that turns portable Sigma rules into Splunk, Elastic, QRadar, Sentinel, and dozens of other query languages.
tools.when: Write detection content once and compile it to every SIEM you run; the shared syntax is also easy to unit-test.

tools.name: Sigma CLI
tools.desc: Official SigmaHQ CLI (sigma-cli) that converts, validates, and tests Sigma rules against backend plugins, catching broken syntax and unsupported constructs.
tools.when: Automate rule conversion and linting in CI so bad Sigma never reaches a SIEM.

tools.name: Elastic detection-rules
tools.desc: Elastic's production rule repository with prebuilt and custom Sigma-style rules, plus tooling (detection-rules CLI) to unit-test, version, and package rules for the Elastic Stack.
tools.when: Benchmark your own rule quality against vendor-maintained content and test rules before shipping to Elastic.

tools.name: VECTR
tools.desc: Free purple-team platform (Security Risk Advisors) that tracks red/blue test cases, campaigns, and per-tool detection/prevention outcomes measured against MITRE ATT&CK over time.
tools.when: Record exercise results and trend detection coverage over months so purple-team improvements are measurable.

tools.name: MITRE Attack Flow
tools.desc: Center for Threat-Informed Defense's STIX-based format and tooling for modeling how adversary behaviors chain together within an operation or campaign.
tools.when: Document the full flow of an emulated campaign — not just isolated techniques — for reporting and ATT&CK mapping.

domains.name: Threat Intelligence, Sharing & Detection Engineering
domains.tagline: Enrich your own defenses: ingest STIX/TAXII feeds, aggregate and pivot on IOCs, correlate infrastructure, and write portable detections against standard frameworks.

tools.name: OpenCTI
tools.desc: Open-source threat-intelligence platform built around the STIX 2.x data model: consumes and exports STIX/TAXII 2.0/2.1, correlates entities into a knowledge graph, and ingests from 100+ connectors.
tools.when: Stand up a central intel drive when you want automated feed ingestion (MISP, MITRE, abuse.ch, TAXII collections) correlated into entities, reports, and indicators rather than raw IOC lists.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/OpenCTI-Platform/docker.git && cp .env.sample .env && docker compose up -d

tools.name: MISP
tools.desc: The open-source intelligence sharing platform that stores and exchanges events as STIX/TAXII-compatible objects, syncs with federated communities, and exposes a full REST API for feeding SIEMs and SOARs.
tools.when: Run or sync a MISP instance when you need governed, TLP-aware intel sharing across your team, an ISAC-style community, or a feed-ingestion pipeline that speaks STIX/TAXII 2 out of the box.

tools.name: TAXII 2.0
tools.desc: The OASIS STIX/TAXII 2.x protocol that feed providers and ISACs use to push and pull structured intelligence over REST in API- and collection-based patterns.
tools.when: Connect your SIEM or intel stack to vendor and community TAXII endpoints, or publish your own vetted indicators to partners without building custom transport.
tools.install: preinstalled (protocol spec); pip install stix2 for client ingestion

tools.name: stix2-client
tools.desc: The official OASIS Python library for creating, querying, and consuming STIX 2 objects and TAXII 2.x collections; pairs with cti-python-taxii2-client for polling remote servers.
tools.when: Automate feed pulls in Python: subscribe to a TAXII collection, parse bundles into STIX objects, and hand cleaned indicators to MISP or OpenCTI.

tools.name: TheHive
tools.desc: Collaborative case-management and incident-response platform that ingests MISP events, runs observables through Cortex analyzers, and can export findings back as STIX/TAXII objects (4.x AGPL archived; current 5.x is StrangeBee commercial).
tools.when: Pairs with MISP and Cortex in the classic open-source IR stack when you need a shared investigation workspace with built-in observable workflows.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/StrangeBeeCorp/docker.git && cd docker && docker compose up -d

tools.name: Cortex
tools.desc: Observable analysis and active-response engine that runs 100+ analyzers (OTX, VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB, GreyNoise, etc.) against IPs, domains, files, and hashes, returning structured, exportable reports.
tools.when: Give TheHive or MISP one shared enrichment backend so every platform calls the same analyzers instead of re-implementing vendor API calls.

tools.name: IntelOwl
tools.desc: Self-hosted aggregation engine that runs a file, IP, domain, or hash through 100+ analyzers and pushes structured results out via connectors to MISP, OpenCTI, and YETI.
tools.when: Automate whole-vendor enrichment in one request and sink normalized findings into your STIX-based platforms via its connector layer.

tools.name: MISP
tools.desc: The foundational open threat-intelligence and sharing framework: event-driven IOC correlation, feed syncing, taxonomies, and TLP/org governance across trusted communities.
tools.when: When you need a mature, community-proven place to store, correlate, and share intel with partners — it is the default first platform to stand up.

tools.name: OpenCTI
tools.desc: Graph-based intel framework that treats actors, campaigns, malware, and infrastructure as interconnected entities, ingesting from MISP and dozens of connectors into a STIX-native store.
tools.when: When your team reasons about campaigns and infrastructure relationships rather than flat IOC lists, so a knowledge-graph backend is worth the heavier deploy.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/OpenCTI-Platform/docker.git && cp .env.sample .env && docker compose up -d

tools.name: TheHive
tools.desc: Collaborative incident case management that links alerts, observables, tasks, and Cortex responses in one shared workspace the whole IR team works from.
tools.when: When multiple analysts investigate simultaneous incidents and you need tasking, observables, and audit history in a single pane with MISP/Cortex integration.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/StrangeBeeCorp/docker.git && cd docker && docker compose up -d

tools.name: Cortex
tools.desc: The analysis orchestrator behind TheHive: schedules observables through analyzers and responders, caches results, and exposes them via REST to any calling platform.
tools.when: Attach a single Cortex to MISP and TheHive so enrichment and active-response is centralized, measured, and repeatable across tools.

tools.name: DFIR-IRIS
tools.desc: Open-source incident-response platform with modern case management, timeline pivoting, IOC enumeration, malware-hash handling, and third-party CTI enrichment via resolvers.
tools.when: Prefer a lighter, actively-developed OSS case manager that still publishes to MISP and pulls enrichment, without TheHive's legacy-or-commercial story.

tools.name: AlienVault OTX
tools.desc: Free open threat exchange (AT&T/LevelBlue): subscribe to community pulses, enrich indicators, and sync IOCs via the OTXv2 SDK into MISP, Splunk, or your SIEM.
tools.when: Commercial-grade feeds with zero platform setup: register, grab an API key, and start aggregating community pulses within the hour.

tools.name: VirusTotal
tools.desc: Multivendor malware-scanning and reputation platform: submit files and URLs, query IP/domain/hash reputation, and pivot via its extensive relationships API.
tools.when: Enrich any observable with detection-ratio context and passive-DNS relationships when you already hold an API key.

tools.name: AbuseIPDB
tools.desc: Community-sourced IP-reputation database backed by user reports and abuse reports, exposed through a simple REST API and check endpoints.
tools.when: Quickly score a suspicious source or destination IP before blocking, and let your SIEM auto-check IPs against its report feed.

tools.name: ThreatMiner
tools.desc: Free threat-intelligence portal and API aggregating passive DNS, WHOIS, hashes, SSL certs, URIs, and APT report tags for a single-indicator research view.
tools.when: Pivot an IOC across WHOIS, passive DNS, and sample relationships in one free lookup with a documented v2 API for scripts.

tools.name: GreyNoise
tools.desc: Classifies internet-scan and background-noise traffic so analysts can tell routine scanning from targeted activity, with a free community API.
tools.when: Filter out opportunistic scanners from your alerts: ask 'is this IP just noise?' before burning analyst time on it.

tools.name: URLhaus
tools.desc: abuse.ch's malicious-URL feed: a plain-text URL list plus RPZ, hostfile, and Suricata/Snort rule packs for proxy, firewall, and log matching.
tools.when: Block or hunt URLs in proxy and DNS logs — the plain-text daily list catches malware distribution paths with low false positives.

tools.name: MalwareBazaar
tools.desc: abuse.ch's sample-sharing database: search by hash, signature, or imphash, download binaries, and pull hourly or daily batch hashes for YARA hunts and sandbox feeds.
tools.when: Grab up-to-date reference samples and hashes by tag or malware family to train detections or validate sandbox coverage.

tools.name: ThreatFox
tools.desc: abuse.ch's malware-IOC feed: query and submit IPs, domains, URLs, and hashes tagged to malware families, with CSV/JSON dumps and MISP event exports.
tools.when: Pull current malware IOCs into your SIEM or pivot a domain/IP to its associated family — the fastest 'what is this IOC attached to' lookup.

tools.name: IntelOwl
tools.desc: Self-hosted analyzer aggregation: one request runs a file, IP, domain, or hash through 100+ free and commercial analyzers (OTX, ThreatFox, MalwareBazaar, VirusTotal, GreyNoise, YARA) and chains pivots.
tools.when: Pivot every incoming IOC across your whole vendor stack automatically, or plug it into MISP, OpenCTI, and TheHive for repeatable centralized enrichment.

tools.name: Pulsedive
tools.desc: Free IOC portal combining passive and active scans, risk scores, ATT&CK tags, and a pivot 'Explore' query language, plus a browser extension for on-page enrichment.
tools.when: Enrich an indicator with risk scores and relationship pivots without standing up a platform — free account, pivot graphs, and exports for fast triage.

tools.name: SecurityTrails
tools.desc: Passive DNS history and subdomain API with a no-key free tier: see every hostname an IP ever resolved and every IP a domain has used.
tools.when: Spot old dev/staging infrastructure or infrastructure churn by replaying DNS history that no longer resolves via live queries.

tools.name: PassiveTotal
tools.desc: RiskIQ's passive-DNS and infrastructure-pivoting workbench whose legacy portal is retiring into Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence (retired 2026); its DNS-history datasets live on in MDTI.
tools.when: Only as a historical reference or for old integrations — use Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence for RiskIQ-class passive-DNS pivot data going forward.
tools.install: preinstalled (web) - retired; successor requires M365 Defender TI license

tools.name: Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence
tools.desc: Microsoft's defender intel platform (successor to RiskIQ/PassiveTotal): passive DNS, certificate/SOAR artifacts, infrastructure-chaining pivots on IPs, domains, and hosts, with a free community tier.
tools.when: When you want RiskIQ-class passive-DNS and infrastructure-chaining datasets and already operate in Defender XDR, Sentinel, or the Microsoft security portal.
tools.install: preinstalled (portal/API; premium licensed, community tier available)

tools.name: DNSDumpster
tools.desc: Free one-click DNS mapping service: resolves a domain to its subdomains, A/NS/MX records, and IPs with a visual map and TXT records.
tools.when: A zero-signup first pass at a domain's DNS surface when you want a quick map before heavier enumeration.

tools.name: Censys
tools.desc: Internet-wide scanning platform searchable by protocol, certificate, banner, and ASN — ideal for TLS-certificate pivoting back to hosts and exposure discovery.
tools.when: Pivot a certificate, hostname, or service banner to every public-facing asset that matches, and monitor your own attack surface over time.
tools.install: preinstalled (web/API; free account with query quota)

tools.name: Shodan
tools.desc: The classic internet-exposure search engine: filters by port, product, vulnerability, ASN, and even CVEs, with API and banner-to-host pivoting.
tools.when: Find every internet-facing instance running a vulnerable service, or check whether an observed IP hosts additional exposed ports and software.
tools.install: preinstalled (web/API; free tier, paid for API)

tools.name: ZoomEye
tools.desc: Chinese internet-wide asset-search engine (Knownsec) covering web applications, devices, and services with components, ports, and country filters.
tools.when: Cross-check Censys/Shodan results against an independent fourth scanning corpus, especially for Asia-heavy infrastructure.

tools.name: FOFA
tools.desc: Internet asset-search platform with a rich query DSL (body, header, port, cert, icon hashes) and bulk API search for infrastructure mapping.
tools.when: When you need expressive full-body searches and favicon based pivoting that cleanly link otherwise unrelated assets.

tools.name: Netlas
tools.desc: Internet-OSINT search engine with cert, DNS, IP, and response-body queries plus a Python SDK, letting you hunt by regex across a large scan index.
tools.when: When you prefer scripting searches in Python or need regex-level body/header pivoting beyond Shodan's filter grammar.

tools.name: Criminal IP
tools.desc: IP-intel and attack-surface search engine with malware, Geopolitics, and internet-scan pivots, plus free API access tiers for resolver lookups.
tools.when: Aggregate IP reputation, exposed-service, and banner intel in one query when reviewing C2 or abuse infra candidates.

tools.name: MISP
tools.desc: MISP's correlation engine links identical and high-fidelity-cluster attributes across every event in your instance and its federated communities.
tools.when: Correlate a suspicious attribute against your event history to find linked campaigns, reused C2, or related infrastructure while investigating an alert.

tools.name: OpenCTI
tools.desc: Uses its STIX knowledge graph to pivot from an indicator to the attack patterns, intrusion sets, and reports that reference it, revealing campaign context.
tools.when: When an IOC is only a starting point and you need the surrounding actor, tooling, and TTP relationships a graph store preserves.

tools.name: Sigma
tools.desc: The SIEM-agnostic YAML rule format: sigma-cli compiles one generic rule to Splunk, Elastic, Loki, QRadar, Sentinel, and dozens of other query languages via conversion backends.
tools.when: Author detection once and ship it anywhere: port a SigmaHQ rule, run sigma convert --target <siem>, and validate the query against logs before tuning.
tools.install: pipx install sigma-cli && git clone https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma

tools.name: YARA
tools.desc: Binary pattern-matching rule engine for malware families and byte-level IOCs; complements SIEM rules when the evidence is a file, not a log.
tools.when: Match dropped samples or artifacts against signature rules, or encode a family signature your feed team cannot express in a log query.

tools.name: Atomic Red Team
tools.desc: Red Canary's adversary-simulation library mapping 700+ ATT&CK techniques to executable test definitions used to prove a detection fires or stays silent.
tools.when: Verify Sigma or SIEM rules against real technique behavior: run the matching atom, watch your alert pipeline, and tune the rule before deployment.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK
tools.desc: The common knowledge base of adversary tactics, techniques, and data sources that Sigma rules, atoms, defenders, and coverage reports all annotate against.
tools.when: Map and measure detection coverage: tag rules with technique IDs, standardize alert vocabulary, or browse technique data sources before writing a rule.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK Navigator
tools.desc: Web-based matrix viewer for layering technique coverage across your detections, with layers you can save as JSON and share between teams.
tools.when: Visualize and report which techniques your Sigma/atomic coverage addresses and which gaps remain in a browsable, shareable matrix layer.
